explicit_propositions.text: There were four baptisms in the first service.
God desires to dwell with His people, as illustrated by the construction of the tabernacle.
Jesus healed ten lepers in the story recorded in Luke 17:11–19.
Only one of the ten lepers returned to thank Jesus.
The returning leper was a Samaritan.
The baptized individuals were aged nine to twelve.
The Israelites freely offered materials for the tabernacle in Exodus 35.
The Israelites’ offerings exceeded the needs for the tabernacle’s construction.
The children sat quietly and took sermon notes with their Bibles open.
Generosity flows naturally from a thankful heart.

assumptions.text: A heartfelt expression of gratitude is necessary to experience God's presence.
Gratitude should be a consistent posture of Christian life, not limited to holidays.
Ungratefulness weakens spiritual connection with God.
Free-will offerings reflect genuine devotion and are more spiritually valuable than mandated contributions.
Spiritual growth involves active participation in communal acts of worship and service.
The physical act of raising hands during worship signifies openness and surrender to God.
Christians are expected to embody both personal and corporate generosity as a sign of faith.
Communion is a sacramental act that strengthens believers’ relationship with Christ.
Pastoral leadership carries responsibility to model and inspire thankfulness and generosity.
The audience values biblical narratives as relevant to contemporary spiritual challenges.
